thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALARM: eu-west-2 monitoring alert group 'edge-dns-ping' firing (63 events in 5m)
alex (oncall): getting paged now, looking... any known maint?
sam (netops): not that I'm aware of, no scheduled maint in euw2 this hour
alex (oncall): metrics page showing missing probe heartbeats for euw2 probes since ~23:12 UTC, alerts all came at 23:15
incident-bot: monitor logs snippet: 
```
2026-03-14T23:12:07Z probe-eu-west-2 ping missed (no telemetry)
2026-03-14T23:13:08Z probe-eu-west-2 ping missed (no telemetry)
2026-03-14T23:14:09Z probe-eu-west-2 heartbeat suppressed by 'control-plane-maintenance' flag
```
alex (oncall): "suppressed" flag? why would monitoring suppress itself?
sam (netops): hold — we just rolled a control-plane rollback for a kube-apiserver taint in euw2 at 23:10 for quick rollback. Automation sets a temporary suppression to avoid storming alerts. Looks like suppression window didn't unwind when rollback ended.
mike (sre): ok that's suspicious — suppression should be tied to a TTL + explicit unset on success. if unset fails, alerts should still unmute. Need to confirm why prometheus-blackbox didn't resume scrapes.
irene (support): any customer impact? Tickets popping up in support with 503s from customers in EU region as of 23:17
dana (product): customers on Dedicated in euw2 --- early reports of timeouts on LLM request streaming. Need triage for customer-facing comms.
alex (oncall): immediate mitigation: I'm re-enabling probes and forcing a full scrape via monitoring API now. running: 
```
curl -X POST "https://monitoring.internal/api/v1/suppressions/clear" -d '{"scope":"eu-west-2","reason":"emergency_enable"}'
# then trigger check
curl -X POST "https://monitoring.internal/api/v1/scrape/blackbox/eu-west-2/trigger"
```
sam (netops): if that fails, we can short-circuit by reconfiguring routing to fallback region for known affected load balancers. but prefer to restore monitoring first so we understand impact.
alex (oncall): cleared suppression, triggered scrape. Monitoring returned: 120 probes succeeded, 7 failed (transient). alert group now reduced.
incident-bot: ALERT STATUS: resolved (alerts cleared) at 23:25 UTC; note: suppression flag removed manually by alex (oncall)
mike (sre): leaving this open for postmortem. we need to know: why suppression persisted after rollback? also why did support see 503s if monitoring was suppressed (i.e., suppression should not affect real traffic)
sam (netops): initial hypothesis: control-plane rollback touched an automation-runbook that sets suppression in two places: monitoring and alert-router. alert-router had stale state and didn't update route fallback rules; some LB health checks failed because of transient control-plane api flakiness. that caused downstream 503s.
irene (support): opened incident ticket INC-2026-0892, added list of affected customers and timestamps; first support inbound 23:17 UTC, severity P2 for now.
dana (product): drafting a short note to affected customers: "We briefly suppressed some internal monitoring during a control-plane rollback which delayed detection; some customers experienced request timeouts in eu-west-2 between 23:15-23:25 UTC. We're investigating and will share root cause."
mike (sre): action items (short):
- sam: root cause drill on automation runbook that sets suppression (owner)
- alex: write a rollback playbook step to verify suppression TTL/unset (owner)
- infra: add heartbeat for suppressed probes that still surfaces non-suppressed health when service errors occur (owner: mike)
- support: customer comms + update INC ticket (owner: irene)
- eng-oncall: add runbook entry about forced-unsuppress endpoint and how to verify scrapes (owner: alex)

sam (netops): I'll post the automation snippet that sets suppression. it uses the job-run id as a key but TTL logic uses job completion signal which didn't arrive due to race. will push patch to clear-on-exit + backstop TTL.
alex (oncall): handing off to mike for overnight follow-up, I'm heading offline in 12m. mike, please own the postmortem and update the incident board.
mike (sre): acknowledged — I'll take it. planning postmortem template: timeline, root cause, impact (customers + internal monitoring gap), remediation, and test plan to prevent recurrence.
irene (support): leaving notes for customer success on next steps for outreach.
incident-bot: Handoff: alex -> mike at 23:37 UTC
alex (oncall): thanks all. closing short-lived paging loop but keeping thread open for postmortem updates. :thumbsup:
